chapter_title: Concerning the Ad[vent] of the Apostle.

fills.notes: Paophi is being paralleled to Parmuthi: neither occurs (i.e., is suitable/appointed) in every month. Verb must match 'occurs' just used for Parmuthi.
The logic is seasonal appointment: a given month/season is 'appointed' for a given work (grain vs fruit). Old substrate speaks in terms of fixed order/season rather than exhortation.
Farmers know the ordered cycle: seasons and their correspondential labors. ‘order’ fits oldest-layer register (cosmic order).
They know (1) vegetables, (2) their growth, (3) cropping-time. Triadic agrarian knowledge mirrors correspondential science (state→form→effect).
Balances the phrase: “vegetables and the … season” → “vegetables and the (appointed) season of each.”
Transition “and they … to Paophi” requires a verb of bringing/carrying the produce into the Paophi stage (fruit month).
Negative contrast: farmer and Parmuthi—he does not sow in Parmuthi; he harvests then. Fits the ensuing conditional ‘if he will come and sow…’ as an improper timing.
If sown in the wrong season, it will not become cereal. Matches agricultural correspondence: time/season as spiritual state prerequisite.
He is involved from the beginning: he takes/receives a seed and toils. ‘receive’ fits correspondential influx into ultimates.
Parallel construction: farmer / gardener. Requires resumptive phrase introducing gardener as a second image.
Gardener tends fruits; key action is watering before ripening/picking. Oldest layer stays concrete in the image.
Paragraph explains apostolic cycle: sent long before appearing; matches ¶8-¶9. The indefinite subject must be ‘apostle’.
“many years before … the world” → before he comes to/into the world. Straightforward temporal descent motif.
Journey ‘below’ is into the depths (opposite the heights). Standard cosmological vertical axis.
Oldest substrate describes freeing forms from constraint; ‘bonds’ matches ‘flesh’ as binding/weight in ultimates.
Completes: “... and [from the bond] of the flesh” as the specific binding from which forms are freed.
Like farmer: first act is sowing; then he begins to tend until harvest month.
“shall begin … tend …” requires infinitival link: begin to tend.
Object and duration needed: tend it until it reaches Parmuthi.
Contrast: harvest in Parmuthi, and not toil then for Paophi-fruits; each has its own season.
Parallel to #4: he may harvest (grain) and not toil (then) for fruits (Paophi).
“this too is how the apostles …” requires ‘are sent’ or ‘work’; ‘are sent’ matches ¶3 opening and ¶12.
Before appearing ‘in flesh’, they act above: freeing forms in the heights (repeated in ¶6, ¶12).
Sequence: when they are sent/prepare, then they will appear/begin below. Sets up ¶9 descent into flesh.
“he shall … free above, first” → he shall make its form free above first (church-form). Echoes ¶6/¶12 phrasing.
At birth in flesh, apostle comes down and at once releases (loosens) it from the binding condition; matches ¶12 ‘releases his church’.
“in the … which comes out from the …” → in the bond which comes out from the flesh. Binding imagery is consistent.
What comes out from the bond is ‘the flesh’; then ‘it is raised up’. Keeps tight correspondence: from flesh to greatness (height).
He remains until the season appointed for him; phrasing of recognition/knowing aligns with correspondential ‘season’ as state of readiness.
“world will come to his …” is a limit/measure/term. Old substrate uses measure/order language.
Connects clauses: when season matures, he is raised up … and he leaves his church.
Even after departure he still helps: he is not far from his church. Avoids later devotional tone while stating continuance of influence.
He ‘goes on before them …’ naturally takes ‘in the way’ (as guide/leader).
He shall not take part in secret: i.e., not take part in the hidden labor once raised, until church reaches its change/season. Keeps impersonal process-language.
“until his church … change it …” requires reaching/attaining the change (its appointed transformation).
The ‘change’ is into another state (degree). Old substrate emphasizes discrete degrees/state-change.
“when his church … he was raised up after it” → when his church has finished (its cycle), he is raised after it.
He rejoices and rests at the last from the labour—echoing farmer’s rest after harvest; keeps image coherence.
Farmer glad of heart in the day when he brings in the harvest; fits idiom and parallel to merchant’s return.
“he and his church …” naturally continues with ‘rejoice’ (then explanation of continuous fruiting/labour).
“for every apostle … in the …” → every apostle labours in the world. Basic substrate statement.
Completes the location of labour: in the world (realm of effects).
“Since … tree, that still is laden with its first fruits” → since a fruit tree… Standard phrase.
Explains picking: first fruits are picked when ripe; then new ones propagated. Keeps the internal cycle logic.
“When they bear these … them on the tree” → bear these and set them on the tree (i.e., establish new fruit).
Second verb needed with ‘them’: ‘set them on the tree’ completes syntax.
Transition from grain to fruits: “When he can finish… Parmuthi! … them in the winter…” needs a resumptive connector. ‘So also’ introduces next seasonal image.
Another apostle sent to another church—relative clause: to another church which he shall make free (above).
Reasserts first action is above. Mirrors ¶6/¶8/¶12 refrain for correspondential order.

fills.fill: it will be born in the flesh
fills.notes: The repeated hinge: after making forms free above, then it is born in flesh; exact echo of ¶9’s “when it will be born in the flesh”.
He comes down and appears in the world (realm of ultimates). Completes descent sequence.
List: conflict, war, and the great …, the battle darkness spread. ‘onslaught’ fits as the intensification between war and battle without importing later moralizing.

“How the light … the darkness” in cosmogony: light is seized/captured by darkness (or darkness seized light). In Manichaean/Iranian structure, Darkness assaults and captures light-substance; ‘seized’ preserves impersonal mechanism.
“through their mingling this universe was set up” presupposes binding/entanglement of light in mixture. ‘was bound in’ matches bondage register used earlier (bonds/flesh).
Dregs/effluent go to the abyss: they are cast down to the abyss. Directional correspondence (downward) is essential.

assessment: Most gaps can be restored at the level of required correspondential mechanics: appointed seasons, descent/ascent, bonds of flesh, and cyclic labour/fruiting. Exact wording remains tentative in several places (especially ¶9–¶12 and parts of ¶11) because multiple Coptic-equivalent verbs could fit the same cosmological logic, but the underlying structure (order of seasons; freeing forms above → birth in flesh → release → ascent; mixture as binding) tightly constrains the semantic field.
